# PRP: Comprehensive Test Suite for job_matcher v1

## Goal

Write a full pytest test suite for the v1 `job_matcher` pipeline that:

1. Lives in `tests/v1/` — a dedicated directory that mirrors the `v1/` source tree and leaves room for `tests/v2/` later
2. Tests every module in isolation — calling `main()` directly with crafted rows
3. Tests every pure helper function (`parse_salary`, `matched_titles`, `matched_locations`, `dedupe_key`, `lookup_town`, `towns_covered`)
4. Documents all known v1 bugs with `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="v1 bug: ...")` — these tests are **expected to fail on v1 and that is correct**
5. Validates the full pipeline against the 60-row `data/labelled_sample.jsonl` (integration layer)
6. Keeps the existing `tests/test_golden.py` and `tests/test_llm_cap.py` passing without modification

**End state**: `make test` runs green. Passing tests = v1 behaves correctly. `XFAIL` tests = documented bugs (intentionally broken in v1 — they serve as the spec for v2). When v2 fixes a bug, the corresponding xfail flips to `XPASS` and breaks CI until the `xfail` mark is removed.

### Philosophy: xfail tests ARE the spec for v2

v1 is deliberately broken. Many tests will show `XFAIL` in the output — this is not a problem, it is the point. Every `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` test:
- Documents exactly what is wrong and why (via `reason=`)
- Pinpoints which module/function needs changing
- Becomes a regression gate the moment the bug is fixed in v2

---

## Why

- The brief explicitly asks for "well-written tests for the rules & logic you implement"
- The 10 known bugs (documented in NOTES.md) have no test coverage — fixing one in v2 has no regression net
- The labelled sample is the only ground-truth: a test against it tracks accuracy improvements
- Module-level tests make it possible to fix one bug at a time and see immediate pass/fail feedback

---

## What

### Module coverage plan

| File | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `tests/__init__.py` | empty — makes `tests` a package for imports |
| `tests/v1/__init__.py` | empty — makes `tests/v1` a package for imports |
| `tests/v1/helpers.py` | `make_row()`, `read_sli()`, `write_jsonl()` shared helpers |
| `tests/v1/conftest.py` | `ctx`, `profile` pytest fixtures |
| `tests/v1/test_town_lookup.py` | `lookup_town`, `towns_covered` pure functions |
| `tests/v1/test_load_job_feed.py` | `load_job_feed.main()` flows |
| `tests/v1/test_normalise_job_rows.py` | `parse_salary` + `normalise_job_rows.main()` flows |
| `tests/v1/test_drop_duplicate_jobs.py` | `dedupe_key` + `drop_duplicate_jobs.main()` flows |
| `tests/v1/test_resolve_job_town.py` | `resolve_job_town.main()` flows |
| `tests/v1/test_match_jobs.py` | `matched_titles`, `matched_locations` + `match_jobs.main()` flows |
| `tests/v1/test_portal_matches_output.py` | `portal_matches_output.main()` flows |
| `tests/v1/test_labelled_sample.py` | Full pipeline against 60 real labelled jobs |

### Success Criteria

- [ ] `make test` exits 0 — all tests either PASS or XFAIL (no FAILED, no ERROR)
- [ ] Every xfail test has `strict=True` and a "v1 bug:" reason string
- [ ] No new test introduces a network call or LLM API call
- [ ] `ruff check tests/v1/` exits 0 (linting)
- [ ] `tests/test_golden.py` and `tests/test_llm_cap.py` still pass (untouched)

---

## Real Run Data (run `20261020T153054`) — ground truth for integration assertions

These numbers come from running the v1 pipeline on the full 1 529-job feed against `profile_a`. Use them to set concrete baseline assertions in `test_labelled_sample.py` and `test_resolve_job_town.py`.

### Pipeline funnel (exact)

```
Module                    Input   Pass   Rejected    Reason
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
load_job_feed             1529    1529   0
normalise_job_rows        1529    1517   ~12         (silent exception, no SLI entry)
drop_duplicate_jobs       1517    1445   72          DUPLICATE
resolve_job_town          1445       6   1439        UNKNOWN_LOCATION  ← primary bottleneck
match_jobs                   6       2      4        3×COMPANY_NOT_LISTED, 1×NO_TITLE_MATCH
OUTPUT                       2
```

### The 6 jobs that survive resolve_job_town (bare-city names in TOWNS dict)

| job_id  | location  | company              | match_jobs outcome  |
|---------|-----------|----------------------|---------------------|
| J678841 | Wrexham   | Inkwell Copperleaf Group | ✅ PASS (output)  |
| J948846 | Wrexham   | Inkwell Copperleaf Group | ✅ PASS (output)  |
| J775031 | Chester   | Moorside Millrace    | ❌ COMPANY_NOT_LISTED |
| J190105 | Wrexham   | Mersey Ironbridge    | ❌ COMPANY_NOT_LISTED |
| J185944 | Wrexham   | Mersey Ironbridge    | ❌ COMPANY_NOT_LISTED |
| J685745 | Runcorn   | Driftwood Copperleaf | ❌ NO_TITLE_MATCH (title is "Software Engineer III, Digital Pathology…") |

### Location format distribution in the 1 529-job feed

| Format                      | Count | % of feed | v1 outcome                       |
|-----------------------------|-------|-----------|----------------------------------|
| `"City, United Kingdom"`    | 555   | 36.3%     | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION (all)         |
| `""` (empty)                | 420   | 27.5%     | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION (all)         |
| `"N Locations"` placeholder | 337   | 22.0%     | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION (all)         |
| bare city / other           | 205   | 13.4%     | ✅ if city is in TOWNS dict       |
| `"City, GB"` / `"City, UK"` |  12   | 0.8%      | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION (all)         |

**Recoverable jobs if suffix-stripping is fixed:** 104 of the 555 "City, United Kingdom" jobs have a city from `profile_a`'s covered towns. Fixing this single suffix-stripping bug lifts output from 2 → ~50 jobs.

---

## All Needed Context

### Source files — read ALL of these before writing tests

```yaml
- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/load_job_feed.py
  why: REJECTION_REASONS = {"INVALID_JSON", "NOT_AN_OBJECT"}; module name for SLI

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/normalise_job_rows.py
  why: parse_salary function; silent exception swallowing bug; salary_gbp field

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/drop_duplicate_jobs.py
  why: dedupe_key f"{title}|{company}" — the bug; REJECTION_REASONS = {"DUPLICATE"}

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/resolve_job_town.py
  why: lookup_town call; REJECTION_REASONS = {"UNKNOWN_LOCATION"}

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/match_jobs.py
  why: matched_titles (substring, case-sensitive, BUG); matched_locations; three-gate logic

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/portal_matches_output.py
  why: output filename pattern; required output fields; artifact["output_path"]

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/_shared/town_lookup.py
  why: TOWNS dict (limited to ~35 cities); lookup_town; towns_covered logic

- file: v1/shared/observability/sli_observe.py
  why: META_OUTCOME constant; passed(); reject(); sli_observe() writes to run_dir/sli_events.jsonl

- file: v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py
  why: run_dir uses ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR env var; ExecutionResult shape

- file: tests/test_golden.py
  why: PATTERN TO FOLLOW — monkeypatch.setenv("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR"), run_pipeline, tmp_path

- file: tests/test_llm_cap.py
  why: PATTERN TO FOLLOW — monkeypatch, fixture pattern, fake_send pattern

- file: data/golden/jobs_small.jsonl
  why: understand golden job shape; minimal valid row structure

- file: data/golden/user_search_inputs/profile_golden/location_searches.json
  why: profile location shape with sub_region type and includes list

- file: data/labelled_sample.jsonl
  why: 60 rows: {"job_id", "decision": "yes"/"no", "reason", "matched_company", ...}
```

### Known v1 Bugs (from NOTES.md) — each needs an xfail test

| # | Location | Bug |
|---|----------|-----|
| 1 | handler level | No dead-link filter: 404/410 jobs pass through (8 in labelled sample) |
| 2 | `resolve_job_town` | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" → UNKNOWN_LOCATION (suffix not stripped; 555 jobs use this format, 104 have profile cities) |
| 2b | `resolve_job_town` | "Bolton, GB" → UNKNOWN_LOCATION (City, GB/UK suffix variant; 12 jobs in feed) |
| 3 | `resolve_job_town` | "Crewe" → UNKNOWN_LOCATION (Crewe not in TOWNS dict) |
| 4 | `resolve_job_town` | "2 Locations" placeholder → UNKNOWN_LOCATION (337 jobs; never uses structured_job.locations) |
| 5 | `matched_titles` | Case-sensitive: `"controls engineer" in "Senior Controls Engineer"` → False |
| 6 | `matched_titles` | Non-adjacent words: `"Quality Engineer" in "Quality and Warranty Engineer"` → False |
| 7 | `match_jobs` | Company exact match only: "Cobalt Zephyr Holdings" ≠ profile "Cobalt Zephyr" |
| 8 | `normalise_job_rows` | `parse_salary("£50K per Annum")` → `ValueError` from `int("50K per Annum")` |
| 9 | `normalise_job_rows` | Missing "scraped" key silently drops row — no SLI entry recorded |
| 10 | `drop_duplicate_jobs` | Dedup key is `title|company`, not `job_id` — two jobs at same company with same title but different locations are incorrectly merged |

**Missing from TOWNS** (causes v1 bugs): Crewe, Knutsford, Bangor, Bromborough, Ellesmere Port, Macclesfield

**Location formats that always fail v1's exact-match lookup** (concrete examples from the real feed):

Shared helper functions (NOT pytest fixtures — plain module-level functions importable from any test file with `from tests.v1.helpers import ...`):

```python
# tests/v1/helpers.py
from __future__ import annotations
import json
from pathlib import Path
from v1.shared.observability.sli_observe import META_OUTCOME


def make_row(
    job_id: str = "J001",
    title: str = "Controls Engineer",
    company: str = "Acme Corp",
    location: str = "Warrington",
    town: str = "Warrington",
    **kwargs,
) -> dict:
    """Build a minimal normalised row ready for post-normalise modules."""
    return {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "title": title,
        "company": company,
        "location": location,
        "town": town,          # added by resolve_job_town
        "salary_gbp": None,
        "source_url": "",
        "page": {},
        META_OUTCOME: "pass",  # CRITICAL: modules filter on this value
        **kwargs,
    }


def read_sli(tmp_path: Path, trace_id: str = "t") -> list[dict]:
    """Read SLI events written during a module call."""
    path = tmp_path / trace_id / "sli_events.jsonl"
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    return [json.loads(l) for l in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l.strip()]


def write_jsonl(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    """Write rows as JSONL for use in load_job_feed tests."""
    path.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in rows) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
```

# PRP: v2 Skeleton — Scaffold with Normalization and Agent Levels

## Goal

Create a complete, runnable skeleton for `v2/` that:
1. Copies `v1/shared/` into `v2/shared/` with updated import paths — the shared runtime will be maintained independently in v2 going forward.
2. Introduces **two new pipeline levels** on top of v1's stage structure:
   - `stage_normalise` — deterministic normalization of title, company, and location fields
   - `stage_agent` — LLM-backed fallback resolution for rows that deterministic normalization cannot handle
3. Wires all stages into a 4-stage STAGE_GRAPH in `v2/workers/job_matcher/handler.py`.
4. Provides **stub modules** for every new stage: pass-through implementations that satisfy the module contract so the pipeline runs end-to-end from day one.
5. Keeps `make test` (v1 tests) green throughout.
6. Adds a `make run-v2` target.

**End state:** `make run-v2` runs without error, produces the same 2 matches as v1 (skeleton parity), and the scaffold is ready for incremental bug fixes tracked by the `tests/v1/` xfail suite.

---

## Why

- **v1 is deliberately broken**: 10 known bugs (see NOTES.md) make it miss ~48 of ~50 matches. The fixes need a clean home with the right structure.
- **Normalization and agent are the solution architecture**: the root cause is almost entirely in data normalization (resolve_job_town dropping 99.6% of rows). A dedicated `stage_normalise` for deterministic fixes + `stage_agent` for LLM-fallback is the right layering.
- **Shared independence**: `v2/shared/` becomes an independent copy — v1 and v2 can diverge without breaking each other. Future workers in v2 import from `v2.shared`.
- **Scaffold first**: creating the structure before implementing logic lets both pipeline execution and incremental module improvements happen independently. Every xfail test in `tests/v1/` is a spec card for a future v2 module fix.

# PRP: v2 Skeleton — Scaffold with Normalization and Agent Levels

## Goal

Create a complete, runnable skeleton for `v2/` that:
1. Copies `v1/shared/` into `v2/shared/` with updated import paths — the shared runtime will be maintained independently in v2 going forward.
2. Introduces **two new pipeline levels** on top of v1's stage structure:
   - `stage_normalise` — deterministic normalization of title, company, and location fields
   - `stage_agent` — LLM-backed fallback resolution for rows that deterministic normalization cannot handle
3. Wires all stages into a 4-stage STAGE_GRAPH in `v2/workers/job_matcher/handler.py`.
4. Provides **stub modules** for every new stage: pass-through implementations that satisfy the module contract so the pipeline runs end-to-end from day one.
5. Keeps `make test` (v1 tests) green throughout.
6. Adds a `make run-v2` target.

**End state:** `make run-v2` runs without error, produces the same 2 matches as v1 (skeleton parity), and the scaffold is ready for incremental bug fixes tracked by the `tests/v1/` xfail suite.

---

## Why

- **v1 is deliberately broken**: 10 known bugs (see NOTES.md) make it miss ~48 of ~50 matches. The fixes need a clean home with the right structure.
- **Normalization and agent are the solution architecture**: the root cause is almost entirely in data normalization (resolve_job_town dropping 99.6% of rows). A dedicated `stage_normalise` for deterministic fixes + `stage_agent` for LLM-fallback is the right layering.
- **Shared independence**: `v2/shared/` becomes an independent copy — v1 and v2 can diverge without breaking each other. Future workers in v2 import from `v2.shared`.
- **Scaffold first**: creating the structure before implementing logic lets both pipeline execution and incremental module improvements happen independently. Every xfail test in `tests/v1/` is a spec card for a future v2 module fix.

---

### Pipeline architecture change (v1 → v2)

```
v1 STAGE_GRAPH                     v2 STAGE_GRAPH
──────────────                     ──────────────
stage_clean_jobs                   stage_clean_jobs     ← same + filter_dead_links added
  load_job_feed                      load_job_feed

The match stage v2 uses `row["resolved_title"]` and `row["resolved_company"]` when present, falling back to `row["title"]` and `row["company"]`.

MODULE_TYPE = "filter"

def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")

## Architecture Notes (for future PRPs)

### What each stub becomes eventually

| Stub module | Future PRP target | Fixes bugs from NOTES.md |
|-------------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| `filter_dead_links` | Already real — done here | Bug #1 |
| `resolve_location` | Suffix stripping + TOWNS expansion + structured_job fallback | Bugs #2, #6, #7 |
| `resolve_title` | Priority chain: structured_job.title > title_tag > h1 > scraped | Bug #3 |
| `resolve_company` | Multi-field lookup + legal suffix stripping | Bug #5 |
| `agent_resolve_location` | LLM city extraction for ambiguous strings | Bugs #2 residual |
| `match_jobs` | Word-by-word title matching, case/punct insensitive | Bug #4 |
| `normalise_job_rows` | Robust parse_salary + error tagging | Bugs #8, #9 |
| `drop_duplicate_jobs` | Dedup by job_id | Bug #10 |

### Why stage_normalise comes before stage_agent

Deterministic normalization handles 95%+ of cases cheaply. The LLM slot (`stage_agent`) only processes the residual rows that deterministic couldn't resolve — keeping cost at £0 for the skeleton and well under £1 once implemented.

### Why v2/shared is an independent copy (not a shared package)

v1 and v2 must be able to evolve independently. If v2/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py gains new capabilities (e.g., async stage execution), v1 must not be affected. The copy-on-fork approach is deliberate.

# PRP: v2 Skeleton — Scaffold with Normalization and Agent Levels

## Goal

Create a complete, runnable skeleton for `v2/` that:
1. Copies `v1/shared/` into `v2/shared/` with updated import paths — the shared runtime is maintained independently in v2 going forward.
2. Writes the **v2 worker from scratch** (no copy from v1) with the correct module contract.
3. Introduces **two new pipeline levels**:
   - `stage_normalise` — deterministic normalization of title, company, and location fields
   - `stage_agent` — LLM-backed fallback resolution for rows that deterministic normalization cannot handle
4. Wires all stages into a 4-stage STAGE_GRAPH in `v2/workers/job_matcher/handler.py`.
5. Provides **stub modules** for all stages: pass-through implementations satisfying the module contract so the pipeline runs end-to-end from day one.
6. Keeps `make test` (v1 tests) green throughout.
7. Adds a `make run-v2` target.

**End state:** `make run-v2` runs without error, writes `runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl`, and the scaffold is ready for incremental implementation.

**Scope boundary:** `v2/shared/` = copied and adapted from v1. `v2/workers/` = written fresh.

---

## Why

- **v1 is deliberately broken**: 10 known bugs make it miss ~48 of ~50 matches. The fixes need a clean, purpose-built home.
- **Normalization and agent are the solution architecture**: the root cause is data normalization (resolve_job_town drops 99.6% of rows). `stage_normalise` + `stage_agent` is the right layering.
- **Shared independence**: `v2/shared/` diverges freely from v1/shared without breaking v1.
- **Scaffold first**: structure before logic — every stub is a placeholder for a specific bug fix.

---

## What

### Pipeline architecture

```
v2 STAGE_GRAPH
──────────────
stage_clean_jobs      load, dead-link filter, normalise rows, dedup
  load_job_feed
  filter_dead_links     ← NEW (fix bug #1: 404/410 jobs pass through in v1)
  normalise_job_rows
  drop_duplicate_jobs

stage_normalise       ← NORMALIZATION LEVEL
  resolve_location      ← fix bug #2: location string parsing
  resolve_title         ← fix bug #3: scraped title abbreviations
  resolve_company       ← fix bug #5: company name normalization

stage_agent           ← AGENT LEVEL (LLM fallback)
  agent_resolve_location  ← stub; calls llm.ask_json() for unresolved locations

stage_match_jobs
  match_jobs            ← fix bug #4: word-by-word title matching
  portal_matches_output
```

### New row fields added by v2 normalise stage

```python
# After stage_normalise, each row gains:
row["resolved_title"]    # str — best title found (stub: same as row["title"])
row["resolved_company"]  # str — normalized company (stub: same as row["company"])
row["town"]              # str — resolved UK town (same contract as v1 resolve_job_town)
row["region"]            # str
row["country"]           # str
row["used_llm"]          # bool — False initially
```

`match_jobs` reads `row.get("resolved_title", row["title"])` and `row.get("resolved_company", row["company"])` so stubs degrade gracefully.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] `make run-v2` exits 0, writes output file
- [ ] `make test` exits 0 — no regression in v1 tests
- [ ] `ruff check v2/ --fix` exits 0
- [ ] `python -c "from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult"` succeeds
- [ ] All v2 modules have: MODULE_NAME, MODULE_TYPE, REJECTION_REASONS, ERROR_REASONS, WARNING_REASONS, `main()`
- [ ] `tests/v2/__init__.py` exists (empty)

---

## All Needed Context

### Source files to READ (not copy — understand only)

```yaml
- file: v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py
  why: Defines ExecutionResult, StageDefinition, run_stage_loop, run_local_handler —
       these are the runtime primitives every module, stage and handler uses.
       v2/shared/ will be an adapted copy; v2/workers/ code imports from v2.shared.

- file: v1/shared/observability/sli_observe.py
  why: Defines passed(), reject(), sli_observe() — the observability contract
       every module must call sli_observe() ONCE at the end on ALL rows.

- file: v1/shared/patterns/logging.py
  why: get_logger(MODULE_NAME), log_event() — logging pattern every module follows.

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/load_job_feed.py
  why: REFERENCE for module contract structure (MODULE_NAME/TYPE/REASONS, main(), L1/L2 pattern)
       Write v2 version fresh — do not copy.

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/match_jobs.py
  why: REFERENCE for three-gate filter pattern (company → title → location).
       Write v2 version fresh with word-by-word title matching.

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/resolve_job_town.py
  why: REFERENCE for resolve_location.py — same field output contract (town/region/country/used_llm).
       Write v2 version fresh.

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/_shared/town_lookup.py
  why: TOWNS dict and lookup_town/towns_covered functions — copy to v2/_shared/ unchanged
       (no internal v1 imports; pure data + pure functions).

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/handler.py
  why: REFERENCE for handler pattern — v2 handler has 4 stages instead of 2.

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/stages/stage_clean_jobs.py
  why: REFERENCE for stage boilerplate (STAGE_NAME, STAGE_GRAPH, schemas, main()).

- file: OUTPUT_FORMAT.json
  why: Canonical matching rules and output field contract.
       Company: fuzzy, across page fields, strip legal suffixes.
       Title: every word present in any order, case/punct insensitive.
       Location: city covers includes; sub_region covers towns inside it; remote covers remote jobs.

- file: NOTES.md
  why: Ground-truth analysis — 10 known v1 bugs, data statistics, pipeline funnel numbers.
       The 10 bugs are the spec for v2 module implementations.
```

### Current codebase tree

```
v1/
  shared/
    api_calls/{__init__,llm}.py
    observability/sli_observe.py
    patterns/{logging,worker_runtime}.py
    schemas/job_matcher/{__init__,v1}.py
    schemas/pipeline_start_takehome/{__init__,v1}.py

    _shared/{__init__,town_lookup}.py

tests/
  test_golden.py   test_llm_cap.py

pyproject.toml
Makefile

    schemas/pipeline_start_takehome/v1.py copy unchanged
  workers/                                ← ALL WRITTEN FRESH
    __init__.py
    job_matcher/
      __init__.py
      handler.py                          fresh — 4-stage STAGE_GRAPH
      _shared/

        town_lookup.py                    copy from v1 _shared (no internal imports)
      stages/
        __init__.py
        stage_clean_jobs.py               fresh — 4 modules
        stage_normalise.py                fresh — 3 modules (NEW LEVEL)
        stage_agent.py                    fresh — 1 module (NEW LEVEL)
        stage_match_jobs.py               fresh — 2 modules
      modules/
        __init__.py
        load_job_feed.py                  fresh stub
        filter_dead_links.py              fresh (real implementation)
        normalise_job_rows.py             fresh stub
        drop_duplicate_jobs.py            fresh stub
        resolve_location.py               fresh stub (normalization level)
        resolve_title.py                  fresh stub (normalization level)
        resolve_company.py                fresh stub (normalization level)
        agent_resolve_location.py         fresh stub (agent level)
        match_jobs.py                     fresh stub (match level)
        portal_matches_output.py          fresh stub (match level)
tests/
  v2/__init__.py                          new empty — ready for future v2 tests
Makefile                                  + run-v2 target
pyproject.toml                            + "v2*" in packages.find
```

### Known Gotchas

```python
# CRITICAL: v2/shared/ imports use "v2." prefix — never "v1."
# Only 3 shared files need edits when copied:
#   v2/shared/observability/sli_observe.py       → 1 change
#   v2/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py         → 2 changes
#   v2/shared/schemas/job_matcher/v1.py          → 1 change

# Without this, "from v2.shared..." raises ModuleNotFoundError at runtime.

# It's the one exception — it's pure data/functions, not a "worker" in the v1 sense.

MODULE_TYPE = "transform" | "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS: set[str] = {"REASON_A", ...}  # or set() if no rejections
ERROR_REASONS: set[str] = set()
WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()

# WRONG: sli_observe(kept, ...)
# RIGHT: sli_observe(rows, ...)  then return kept

# GOTCHA: stub modules must set META_OUTCOME = "pass" on rows that arrive without it
# load_job_feed sets it; all downstream modules assume it's set.

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"COMPANY_NOT_LISTED", "NO_TITLE_MATCH", "NO_LOCATION_MATCH"}

import re

_LEGAL_SUFFIXES = re.compile(
    r"\s+(ltd|limited|plc|group|holdings|international|uk)\s*$", re.IGNORECASE
)

def _normalise_name(name: str) -> str:
    name = name.lower().strip()
    name = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", "", name)
    name = _LEGAL_SUFFIXES.sub("", name)
    name = re.sub(r"^the\s+", "", name)
    return name.strip()

def _words(title: str) -> set[str]:
    tokens = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", " ", title.lower()).split()
    # strip trailing plural 's'
    return {t.rstrip("s") for t in tokens}

def matched_titles(job_title: str, profile_titles: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Every word of each profile title must appear in job_title (any order, case-insensitive)."""
    job_words = _words(job_title)
    return [t for t in profile_titles if _words(t) <= job_words]

def matched_companies(job_company: str, profile_companies: set[str]) -> str | None:
    """Return the profile company name that matches (after suffix normalisation), or None."""
    norm_job = _normalise_name(job_company)
    for c in profile_companies:
        if _normalise_name(c) == norm_job:
            return c
    return None

def main(context, prev_data):
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    profile = context["profile"]
    profile_companies = {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}
    rows = [dict(r) for r in prev_data]   # copy so same rows can run multiple profiles
    for row in rows:
        job_company = row.get("resolved_company") or row.get("company", "")
        job_title   = row.get("resolved_title")   or row.get("title", "")
        matched_co = matched_companies(job_company, profile_companies)
        if matched_co is None:
            reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
            continue
        titles = matched_titles(job_title, profile["titles"])
        if not titles:
            reject(row, "NO_TITLE_MATCH")
            continue
        locations = [loc["name"] for loc in profile["locations"]
                     if row.get("town", "") in towns_covered(loc)]
        if not locations:
            reject(row, "NO_LOCATION_MATCH")
            continue
        row["matched_company"]   = matched_co
        row["matched_job_title"] = titles
        row["matched_location"]  = locations
        row["reason"]            = f"{job_title} at {matched_co}, in {row.get('town', '')}"
    kept = passed(rows)
    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
                           data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={})

## Goal

Create a complete, runnable skeleton for `v2/` that:
1. Copies `v1/shared/` into `v2/shared/` with updated import paths — the shared runtime is maintained independently in v2 going forward.
2. Writes the **v2 worker from scratch** (no copy from v1) with the correct module contract.
3. Introduces **two new pipeline levels**:
   - `stage_normalise` — deterministic normalization of title, company, and location fields
   - `stage_agent` — LLM-backed fallback resolution for rows that deterministic normalization cannot handle
4. Wires all stages into a 4-stage STAGE_GRAPH in `v2/workers/job_matcher/handler.py`.
5. Provides **stub modules** for all stages: pass-through implementations satisfying the module contract so the pipeline runs end-to-end from day one.
6. Keeps `make test` (v1 tests) green throughout.
7. Adds a `make run-v2` target.

**End state:** `make run-v2` runs without error, writes `runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl`, and the scaffold is ready for incremental implementation.

**Scope boundary:** `v2/shared/` = copied and adapted from v1. `v2/workers/` = written fresh.

---

## Why

- **v1 is deliberately broken**: 10 known bugs make it miss ~48 of ~50 matches. The fixes need a clean, purpose-built home.
- **Normalization and agent are the solution architecture**: the root cause is data normalization (resolve_job_town drops 99.6% of rows). `stage_normalise` + `stage_agent` is the right layering.
- **Shared independence**: `v2/shared/` diverges freely from v1/shared without breaking v1.
- **Scaffold first**: structure before logic — every stub is a placeholder for a specific bug fix.

---

## What

### Pipeline architecture

```
v2 STAGE_GRAPH
──────────────
stage_clean_jobs      load, dead-link filter, normalise rows, dedup
  load_job_feed
  filter_dead_links     ← NEW (fix bug #1: 404/410 jobs pass through in v1)
  normalise_job_rows
  drop_duplicate_jobs

stage_normalise       ← NORMALIZATION LEVEL
  resolve_location      ← fix bug #2: location string parsing
  resolve_title         ← fix bug #3: scraped title abbreviations
  resolve_company       ← fix bug #5: company name normalization

stage_agent           ← AGENT LEVEL (LLM fallback)
  agent_resolve_location  ← stub; calls llm.ask_json() for unresolved locations

stage_match_jobs
  match_jobs            ← fix bug #4: word-by-word title matching
  portal_matches_output
```

### New row fields added by v2 normalise stage

```python
# After stage_normalise, each row gains:
row["resolved_title"]    # str — best title found (stub: same as row["title"])
row["resolved_company"]  # str — normalized company (stub: same as row["company"])
row["town"]              # str — resolved UK town (same contract as v1 resolve_job_town)
row["region"]            # str
row["country"]           # str
row["used_llm"]          # bool — False initially
```

`match_jobs` reads `row.get("resolved_title", row["title"])` and `row.get("resolved_company", row["company"])` so stubs degrade gracefully.

### Known Gotchas

```python
# CRITICAL: v2/shared/ imports use "v2." prefix — never "v1."
# Only 3 shared files need edits when copied:
#   v2/shared/observability/sli_observe.py       → 1 change
#   v2/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py         → 2 changes
#   v2/shared/schemas/job_matcher/v1.py          → 1 change

# CRITICAL: pyproject.toml must include "v2*" in packages.find
# Without this, "from v2.shared..." raises ModuleNotFoundError at runtime.

# CRITICAL: v2/_shared/town_lookup.py is a COPY (it has no internal imports)
# It's the one exception — it's pure data/functions, not a "worker" in the v1 sense.

# CRITICAL: module contract — every module file must have at the top:
MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__<snake_case_name>"    # used in SLI events
MODULE_TYPE = "transform" | "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS: set[str] = {"REASON_A", ...}  # or set() if no rejections
ERROR_REASONS: set[str] = set()
WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()

# CRITICAL: sli_observe must be called on ALL rows (passed + rejected)
# WRONG: sli_observe(kept, ...)
# RIGHT: sli_observe(rows, ...)  then return kept

# GOTCHA: stub modules must set META_OUTCOME = "pass" on rows that arrive without it
# load_job_feed sets it; all downstream modules assume it's set.
# Stubs that don't filter can just pass prev_data through without touching META_OUTCOME.

# GOTCHA: resolve_location must produce row["town"], row["region"], row["country"], row["used_llm"]
# match_jobs reads row["town"] directly — this field name must not change.
# For the skeleton: use the same lookup_town() logic as v1 resolve_job_town.

# GOTCHA: filter_dead_links is NOT a stub — implement it for real (5 lines of logic)
# It fixes the single most-impactful v1 bug with trivial code.

# GOTCHA: portal_matches_output must write the output file and return artifacts={"output_path": str(out)}
# The handler's run_pipeline() reads context["output_path"] from this artifact — it's contract-critical.

# GOTCHA: stage boilerplate — every stage.py has:
#   STAGE_NAME, STAGE_GRAPH, INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA, OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA, main()
# The schemas only need to declare fields the stage actually uses/produces.
# Minimal safe schema: just require trace_id in both input and output.
```

### Per-task pseudocode

```python
# ── Task 5: load_job_feed.py ──────────────────────────────────────────
MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__load_job_feed"
MODULE_TYPE = "transform"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"INVALID_JSON", "NOT_AN_OBJECT"}

def main(context, prev_data):
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    rows: list[dict] = []
    with Path(context["jobs_path"]).open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line_no, line in enumerate(f, start=1):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            try:
                raw = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                rows.append({"_line": line_no, META_OUTCOME: "rejected",
                             META_REJECTION_REASON: "INVALID_JSON"})
                continue
            if not isinstance(raw, dict):
                rows.append({"_line": line_no, META_OUTCOME: "rejected",
                             META_REJECTION_REASON: "NOT_AN_OBJECT"})
                continue
            rows.append({**raw, META_OUTCOME: "pass"})
    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
                           data=passed(rows), artifacts={}, metrics={})

# ── Task 6: filter_dead_links.py ─────────────────────────────────────
MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__filter_dead_links"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"DEAD_LINK"}

def main(context, prev_data):
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    for row in prev_data:
        if row.get("page", {}).get("http_status") in (404, 410):
            reject(row, "DEAD_LINK")
    kept = passed(prev_data)
    sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
                           data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={})

# ── Task 7: normalise_job_rows.py ─────────────────────────────────────
MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__normalise_job_rows"
MODULE_TYPE = "transform"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"MALFORMED_ROW"}

def parse_salary(value) -> int | None:
    # Stub: returns None for any non-integer value (safe, no crash)
    # TODO: handle "£50K", "45,000", range strings
    if value is None or value == "":
        return None
    try:
        return int(str(value).replace("£", "").replace(",", "").strip())
    except ValueError:
        return None

def main(context, prev_data):
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for raw in prev_data:
        scraped = raw.get("scraped")
        if not isinstance(scraped, dict):
            row = {**raw, META_OUTCOME: "rejected",
                   META_REJECTION_REASON: "MALFORMED_ROW"}
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        rows.append({
            "job_id":     raw["job_id"],
            "title":      scraped.get("title", "").strip(),
            "company":    scraped.get("company", "").strip(),
            "location":   scraped.get("location", "").strip(),
            "salary_gbp": parse_salary(scraped.get("salary")),
            "source_url": raw.get("source_url") or "",
            "page":       raw.get("page") or {},
            META_OUTCOME: "pass",
        })
    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
                           data=passed(rows), artifacts={}, metrics={})

# ── Task 8: drop_duplicate_jobs.py ────────────────────────────────────
MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__drop_duplicate_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"DUPLICATE"}

def main(context, prev_data):
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for row in prev_data:
        key = row["job_id"]           # v2 fix: dedup by job_id, not title|company
        if key in seen:
            reject(row, "DUPLICATE")
        seen.add(key)
    kept = passed(prev_data)
    sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
                           data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={})

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"COMPANY_NOT_LISTED", "NO_TITLE_MATCH", "NO_LOCATION_MATCH"}

import re

_LEGAL_SUFFIXES = re.compile(
    r"\s+(ltd|limited|plc|group|holdings|international|uk)\s*$", re.IGNORECASE
)

def _normalise_name(name: str) -> str:
    name = name.lower().strip()
    name = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", "", name)
    name = _LEGAL_SUFFIXES.sub("", name)
    name = re.sub(r"^the\s+", "", name)
    return name.strip()

def _words(title: str) -> set[str]:
    tokens = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", " ", title.lower()).split()
    # strip trailing plural 's'
    return {t.rstrip("s") for t in tokens}

def matched_titles(job_title: str, profile_titles: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Every word of each profile title must appear in job_title (any order, case-insensitive)."""
    job_words = _words(job_title)
    return [t for t in profile_titles if _words(t) <= job_words]

def matched_companies(job_company: str, profile_companies: set[str]) -> str | None:
    """Return the profile company name that matches (after suffix normalisation), or None."""
    norm_job = _normalise_name(job_company)
    for c in profile_companies:
        if _normalise_name(c) == norm_job:
            return c
    return None

def main(context, prev_data):
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    profile = context["profile"]
    profile_companies = {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}
    rows = [dict(r) for r in prev_data]   # copy so same rows can run multiple profiles
    for row in rows:
        job_company = row.get("resolved_company") or row.get("company", "")
        job_title   = row.get("resolved_title")   or row.get("title", "")
        matched_co = matched_companies(job_company, profile_companies)
        if matched_co is None:
            reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
            continue
        titles = matched_titles(job_title, profile["titles"])
        if not titles:
            reject(row, "NO_TITLE_MATCH")
            continue
        locations = [loc["name"] for loc in profile["locations"]
                     if row.get("town", "") in towns_covered(loc)]
        if not locations:
            reject(row, "NO_LOCATION_MATCH")
            continue
        row["matched_company"]   = matched_co
        row["matched_job_title"] = titles
        row["matched_location"]  = locations
        row["reason"]            = f"{job_title} at {matched_co}, in {row.get('town', '')}"
    kept = passed(rows)
    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
                           data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={})

def main(context, prev_data):
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    profile = context["profile"]
    profile_companies = {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}
    rows = [dict(r) for r in prev_data]   # copy so same rows can run multiple profiles
    for row in rows:
        job_company = row.get("resolved_company") or row.get("company", "")
        job_title   = row.get("resolved_title")   or row.get("title", "")
        matched_co = matched_companies(job_company, profile_companies)
        if matched_co is None:
            reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
            continue
        titles = matched_titles(job_title, profile["titles"])
        if not titles:
            reject(row, "NO_TITLE_MATCH")
            continue
        locations = [loc["name"] for loc in profile["locations"]
                     if row.get("town", "") in towns_covered(loc)]
        if not locations:
            reject(row, "NO_LOCATION_MATCH")
            continue
        row["matched_company"]   = matched_co
        row["matched_job_title"] = titles
        row["matched_location"]  = locations
        row["reason"]            = f"{job_title} at {matched_co}, in {row.get('town', '')}"
    kept = passed(rows)
    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
                           data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={})

The user is asking why `town_lookup.py` is needed in v2. This is a good question. Let me think about it.

`town_lookup.py` contains:
1. A `TOWNS` dict — hardcoded mapping of UK town names to region/country
2. `lookup_town(text)` — exact case-insensitive lookup
3. `towns_covered(location)` — expands a profile location to the set of towns it covers

In v1, `resolve_job_town.py` uses `lookup_town()` and `match_jobs.py` uses `towns_covered()`.

In v2:
- `normalization/resolve_location.py` will use `lookup_town()` (the stub currently does this)
- `modules/match_jobs.py` will use `towns_covered()`

So it is still needed — but the user's question might really be probing whether the TOWNS dict approach itself should change, move elsewhere, or live in normalization/ instead of _shared/, especially since it's known to be incomplete (missing towns like Crewe). Even though resolve_location.py will eventually add suffix-stripping and structured_job fallback logic beyond the dict, match_jobs.py still depends on towns_covered(), so the module isn't going away.

The dict actually serves two distinct roles: `lookup_town()` resolves job-side locations and will likely get superseded by proper normalization, while `towns_covered()` expands a profile's location entry into matching towns for comparison and remains essential. So for the skeleton, I'll keep towns_covered() as the backbone for profile-side matching, while treating lookup_town() as a fallback that normalization will gradually replace.

Resolved against the profile's includes list directly, bypassing the TOWNS dict entirely, or alternatively the dict could be expanded into a proper UK towns database. So `towns_covered()` seems genuinely necessary as profile-side logic, while `lookup_town()` and its TOWNS dict might be better off folded directly into resolve_location.py rather than living in `_shared/` — it's really a design call. I'll give a short, direct answer covering what it's used for and what might change.

# Brief (перевод)

## Задача

### Контекст

Рекрутер задаёт поисковые параметры в `data\user_search_inputs`:

* **Компании** — карьерные страницы которых нужно искать (например, Deloitte)
* **Должности** — которые нужно искать (например, Senior Consultant)
* **Локации** — где нужно найти вакансии (например, United Kingdom)

### Суть задачи

Нужно сопоставить 1 500 реальных вакансий из `data\jobs_raw.jsonl` с этими поисковыми параметрами. Этот процесс стоит после скрапинга карьерных страниц — все данные локальные, живые запросы  **не требуются** .

Мы предоставили версию 1 в `v1\workers\job_matcher` — базовый каркас для старта, однако он намеренно сломан и точно не сопоставляет вакансии. Подробнее — в README.

Рекрутеры получают комиссию 15–30% от зарплаты: отправить кандидата на позицию £100K — это £15–30K для рекрутингового агентства. В рекрутинге критична скорость — карьерные страницы публикуют вакансии раньше, чем они появляются на LinkedIn, Indeed, Reed и т.д. Успешный скрапинг и точная фильтрация создают сильные лиды для рекрутеров.

### Что оценивается

Цель — создать систему, которая совпадает с ответами нашего производственного job_matcher на ≥ 90% на приватном датасете.

Важнее результата —  **процесс** :

* Чистый, лаконичный код: небольшое, хорошо ограниченное решение с явными компромиссами лучше большого
* Эффективность: учитывайте сложность по времени и памяти — должно обрабатывать 200 000 вакансий за 20 минут
* Хорошо написанные тесты для реализованных правил и логики
* Процесс: коммиты часто и понемногу — важно видеть хронологию

Предполагается использование AI-инструментов, но `PLAN.md`, `DECISIONS.md` и `NOTES.md` должны быть написаны лаконично и своими словами.

---

## Система сборки

### Правила сопоставления

* Сопоставление бинарное: вакансия попадает в список только если совпадают все три — компания, хотя бы одна должность, хотя бы одна локация
* Точность важнее объёма — главная ценность продукта в отсутствии шума
* Вакансия в нескольких местах проходит, если хотя бы одно совпадает: «Bristol, Manchester» при поиске по «Bristol» — это проход
* Компания должна быть где-то на странице вакансии (указанная компания, заголовок, title tag, URL или текст страницы) — это лишь слабая проверка, что мы на правильной карьерной странице
* Рекрутеру нужно подтверждение, что вакансия активна. Битая ссылка (404/410) никогда не попадает в список
* Полные определения: [OUTPUT_FORMAT.json](vscode-webview://1v39apq4avr8iiqjj1oroimd5ubhdvs21bt23kri7kp88fv067is/OUTPUT_FORMAT.json)

### Технические предпочтения

* API LLM будет предоставлен, см. `.env.example`. Это живые вызовы с ограниченным бюджетом — **цель £1, максимум £3**
* Использование LLM — на ваше усмотрение, но учитывайте стоимость по сравнению с кодом
* Должно работать на 200 000 вакансий за 20 минут
* `tools/make_scale_feed.py` генерирует тестовый датасет 200 000 вакансий из `data/jobs_raw.jsonl`
* Скрапинг не выполняется — каждая вакансия уже содержит страницу, которую мы скачали единожды: `page.http_status` и всё что она показала. В данных есть заблокированные страницы, битые ссылки, пустые локации, несоответствия заголовков, неверные компании. Также японские символы в локациях и плейсхолдеры вида «3 Locations» — каждый случай требует обоснованной политики обработки

### 4 фазы (1–2 часа суммарно, без бонусов за превышение)

| Фаза | Время    | Результат                                 |
| -------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Plan     | 15–30 мин | `PLAN.md` — написанный вручную |
| Build    | 15–30 мин | коммиты                                     |
| Tune     | 15–30 мин | коммиты                                     |
| Complete | 15–30 мин | `NOTES.md`                                       |

Записывайте старт и конец в `NOTES.md`, каждое решение — в `DECISIONS.md` по ходу работы. Коммиты — часто и понемногу, не одним разом в конце.

---

## Входные данные

Все входные данные находятся в `data\`.

### Поисковые параметры

Каждый рекрутер имеет папку в `data\user_search_inputs\` (например, `profile_a`) с тремя файлами:

* `company_searches.json` — компании (поле `industry` — только контекст, заполнено примерно наполовину)
* `job_title_searches.json` — должности
* `location_searches.json` — локации с полями: name, country, type и список `includes`

Типы локаций:

* `city` — покрывает своё название и все города из `includes`
* `sub_region` (регион, страна или округ) — покрывает любой город внутри него
* `remote` — покрывает вакансии, где работодатель указывает удалённую/домашнюю работу в этой стране; но вакансия в другой стране никогда не попадает в локацию, как бы город ни назывался

Каждый файл содержит одинаковый `profile_id`, который проставляется на каждой строке вывода. Runtime читает папку через `load_search_inputs` в `v1\shared\patterns\worker_runtime.py`. Оценка производится на другом профиле рекрутера — ничего не должно быть захардкожено под `profile_a`.

### Вакансии

`data\jobs_raw.jsonl` — около 1 500 вакансий, по одной на строку. Каждая содержит:

* `job_id` — копировать в вывод без изменений
* поля `scraped` — title, company, location, salary (часто сокращённые, пустые или неверные)
* `source_url` — анонимизирован, не откроется
* `page` — страница, скачанная единожды: `http_status`, title tag, h1, meta-теги, видимый текст и `structured_job` (факты о вакансии, задекларированные самой страницей: title, company, locations). Любое из этих полей может отсутствовать

### Ответы и тесты

`data\labelled_sample.jsonl` — 60 вакансий с правильным решением (matched_company, matched_job_title, matched_location, reason) — единственный доступный ключ ответов. `data\golden\` — маленький датасет, который уже проходит стартовый код; запускается через `make test`.







# Brief

## The Task

### Background

A recruiter user will provide their search inputs at `data\user_search_inputs`, which are:

- Companies they wish to search the career pages of e.g. Deloitte
- Job titles they wish to search for e.g. Senior Consultant
- Locations they wish to find these roles e.g. United Kingdom

### The Task

This task is matching 1,500 real mass-scraped jobs at `data\jobs_raw.jsonl` to these search inputs. This process is downstream of the career page scraping process, all data provided is local & you are **not** expected to perform any live searches.

We have provided a version 1 located at `v1\workers\job_matcher`, which provides a basic framework to start from, however it is deliberately broken & does not match jobs accurately. See the README for a deeper understanding.

Recruiters are paid a % fee, from 15-30% of a salary, meaning sending a £100K salary Candidate to an open role & then being hired, earning a Recruitment company £15-£30K. Recruitment is critically based off speed, Career Pages are typically the first place a job goes live before hitting job boards such as LinkedIn, Indeed, Reed etc, meaning if we can successfully scrape career pages & filter accurately, this can create strong leads for Recruiters.

### What we're looking for

This task is to create a successfully matching codebase that matches our production job_matcher answers to within 90%, on a dataset we hold privately.

More importantly, we're assessing how you get there:

- Clear, concise code: a small, well-scoped solution with clear trade-offs is better than a big one.
- Efficiency: think about time and space complexity, it must run 200k jobs in under 20 minutes.
- Well-written tests for the rules & logic you implement.
- Your process: commit little and often, it's important for us to see a timeline

We expect AI-assisted coding tools will be used, but make sure PLAN.md, DECISIONS.md & NOTES.md are concisely written documents.

## The Build

### Matching standards

- The matching is pass / fail. A job goes in only when all three match: the company, at least one job title, at least one location.
- Precision matters more than volume, the core selling point of this product is it doesn't produce noise.
- A job in several places is in if ANY of them matches: "Bristol, Manchester" for a recruiter with "Bristol" in their search inputs, this is a pass.
- The company must appear somewhere on the job page (declared company, heading, title tag, URL or body text). That's only a loose validator to ensure we have the correct career page, because the search upstream should have already picked the correct company's career page.
- A recruiter needs evidence the job is live. A dead link (404 / 410) never goes in.
- Full definitions: [OUTPUT_FORMAT.json](OUTPUT_FORMAT.json).

### Engineering preferences

- An LLM API will be provided before the task, see the example at .env.example. These are live API calls from API keys with capped budgets & there will likely be cases where an LLM is required, you should aim for £1 target, £3 max spend.
- The use of LLM matching should be at your discretion, although keep in mind the cost vs matching via code.
- It must run on 200k jobs in under 20 minutes.
- `tools/make_scale_feed.py` builds the 200,000-job test feed from `data/jobs_raw.jsonl`.
- No scraping happens, each job already carries the page we fetched once (`page.http_status` + what it showed). Blocked pages, dead links, blank locations, title mismatches, wrong company on the page. Japanese-script locations and "3 Locations" placeholders are all in that data. Each needs a defensible policy.

### The 4 phases

Plan     - 15-30 minutes - `PLAN.md`, handwritten documents
Build    - 15-30 minutes - commits
Tune     - 15-30 minutes - commits
Complete - 15-30 minutes - `NOTES.md`

1-2 hours total (self-timed), there are no bonus points for exceeding the time limit. Log your start and end in `NOTES.md`, log every decision in `DECISIONS.md` as you make it.

Commit little and often, at every step, not once at the end, we want to see the development of commits over a timeline.

## Your inputs

All inputs live in `data\`.

### Search inputs

Each recruiter has a folder at `data\user_search_inputs\`, e.g. `profile_a`, holding the three searches they set up:
`company_searches.json` lists the companies they recruit for (the industry field is context only & about half filled)
`job_title_searches.json` lists the job titles they place
`location_searches.json` lists where they work, with every location carrying a name, a country, a type & an `includes` list of the towns it covers.

A `city` covers its own name & its includes, a `sub_region` (a region, nation or county) also covers any town inside it, and `remote` covers jobs the employer says are remote or home-based in that country, but a job in another country is never inside a location, whatever the town is called.

Every file carries the same `profile_id`, which goes on every output line, and the starter reads the folder back into one profile for you through `load_search_inputs` in `v1\shared\patterns\worker_runtime.py`. We grade on a different recruiter's folder, so nothing should be hard-coded to `profile_a`.

### The jobs

`data\jobs_raw.jsonl` holds about 1,500 jobs, one per line. Each has a `job_id` to copy to your output unchanged, the `scraped` fields our scraper stored (title, company, location & salary, which are often abbreviated, blank or wrong), the `source_url` it was found at (anonymised, so it will not load), and the `page` exactly as we fetched it once: its `http_status`, then whatever it showed, which is the title tag, the h1, the meta tags, the visible text and `structured_job`, the job facts the page declared itself (title, company & locations). Any of these can be missing or empty.

### Answers & tests

`data\labelled_sample.jsonl` has 60 jobs with the right decision, matched company, job titles & locations, and reason, and is the only answer key you get. `data\golden\` holds a tiny feed & profile the starter already passes, which `make test` runs.

# Create PRP

## Feature file: тебе нужно сделать карказ для версии v2. Проект shared нужно будет скопировать в v2. Он нужен будет в будущем. Мы будем работать с ним. Далее у нас будет уровень agent и normalization. Нам нужно еще пораассуждать. 

Для допллниьельной информации изучи документа  NOTES.md, BRIEF.md

Generate a complete PRP for general feature implementation with thorough research. Ensure context is passed to the AI agent to enable self-validation and iterative refinement. Read the feature file first to understand what needs to be created, how the examples provided help, and any other considerations.

The AI agent only gets the context you are appending to the PRP and training data. Assuma the AI agent has access to the codebase and the same knowledge cutoff as you, so its important that your research findings are included or referenced in the PRP. The Agent has Websearch capabilities, so pass urls to documentation and examples.

## Research Process

1. **Codebase Analysis**
   - Search for similar features/patterns in the codebase
   - Identify files to reference in PRP
   - Note existing conventions to follow
   - Check test patterns for validation approach

2. **External Research**
   - Search for similar features/patterns online
   - Library documentation (include specific URLs)
   - Implementation examples (GitHub/StackOverflow/blogs)
   - Best practices and common pitfalls

3. **User Clarification** (if needed)
   - Specific patterns to mirror and where to find them?
   - Integration requirements and where to find them?

## PRP Generation

Using PRPs/templates/prp_base.md as template:

### Critical Context to Include and pass to the AI agent as part of the PRP
- **Documentation**: URLs with specific sections
- **Code Examples**: Real snippets from codebase
- **Gotchas**: Library quirks, version issues
- **Patterns**: Existing approaches to follow

### Implementation Blueprint
- Start with pseudocode showing approach
- Reference real files for patterns
- Include error handling strategy
- list tasks to be completed to fullfill the PRP in the order they should be completed

### Validation Gates (Must be Executable) eg for python
```bash
# Syntax/Style
ruff check --fix && mypy .

# Unit Tests
uv run pytest tests/ -v

```

*** CRITICAL AFTER YOU ARE DONE RESEARCHING AND EXPLORING THE CODEBASE BEFORE YOU START WRITING THE PRP ***

*** ULTRATHINK ABOUT THE PRP AND PLAN YOUR APPROACH THEN START WRITING THE PRP ***

## Output
Save as: `PRPs/{feature-name}.md`

## Quality Checklist
- [ ] All necessary context included
- [ ] Validation gates are executable by AI
- [ ] References existing patterns
- [ ] Clear implementation path
- [ ] Error handling documented

Score the PRP on a scale of 1-10 (confidence level to succeed in one-pass implementation using claude codes)

Remember: The goal is one-pass implementation success through comprehensive context.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. 3	## Goal
4	
5	Create a complete, runnable skeleton for `v2/` that:
6	
7	1. Copies `v1/shared/` into `v2/shared/` with updated import paths — the shared runtime is maintained independently in v2 going forward.
8	2. Writes the **v2 worker from scratch** (no copy from v1) with the correct module contract.
9	3. Introduces **two new pipeline levels**:
10	   - `stage_normalise` — deterministic normalization of title, company, and location fields
11	   - `stage_agent` — LLM-backed fallback resolution for rows that deterministic normalization cannot handle
12	4. Wires all stages into a 4-stage STAGE_GRAPH in `v2/workers/job_matcher/handler.py`.
13	5. Provides **stub modules** for all stages: pass-through implementations satisfying the module contract so the pipeline runs end-to-end from day one.
14	6. Keeps `make test` (v1 tests) green throughout.
15	7. Adds a `make run-v2` target.

27	- **Shared independence**: `v2/shared/` diverges freely from v1/shared without breaking v1.

403	MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__load_job_feed"
404	MODULE_TYPE = "transform"
405	REJECTION_REASONS = {"INVALID_JSON", "NOT_AN_OBJECT"}
406	
407	def main(context, prev_data):
408	    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
409	    start_time = time.time()
410	    rows: list[dict] = []
411	    with Path(context["jobs_path"]).open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
412	        for line_no, line in enumerate(f, start=1):
413	            if not line.strip():
414	                continue
415	            try:
416	                raw = json.loads(line)
417	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
418	                rows.append({"_line": line_no, META_OUTCOME: "rejected",
419	                             META_REJECTION_REASON: "INVALID_JSON"})
420	                continue
421	            if not isinstance(raw, dict):
422	                rows.append({"_line": line_no, META_OUTCOME: "rejected",
423	                             META_REJECTION_REASON: "NOT_AN_OBJECT"})
424	                continue
425	            rows.append({**raw, META_OUTCOME: "pass"})
426	    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
427	    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
428	                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
429	                           data=passed(rows), artifacts={}, metrics={})

453	def parse_salary(value) -> int | None:
454	    # Stub: returns None for any non-integer value (safe, no crash)
455	    # TODO: handle "£50K", "45,000", range strings
456	    if value is None or value == "":
457	        return None
458	    try:
459	        return int(str(value).replace("£", "").replace(",", "").strip())
460	    except ValueError:
461	        return None

463	def main(context, prev_data):
464	    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
465	    start_time = time.time()

# PRP: v2 Skeleton — Scaffold with Normalization and Agent Levels

## Goal

Create a complete, runnable skeleton for `v2/` that:

1. Copies `v1/shared/` into `v2/shared/` with updated import paths — the shared runtime is maintained independently in v2 going forward.
2. Writes the **v2 worker from scratch** (no copy from v1) with the correct module contract.
3. Introduces **two new pipeline levels**:
   - `stage_normalise` — deterministic normalization of title, company, and location fields
   - `stage_agent` — LLM-backed fallback resolution for rows that deterministic normalization cannot handle
4. Wires all stages into a 4-stage STAGE_GRAPH in `v2/workers/job_matcher/handler.py`.
5. Provides **stub modules** for all stages: pass-through implementations satisfying the module contract so the pipeline runs end-to-end from day one.
6. Keeps `make test` (v1 tests) green throughout.
7. Adds a `make run-v2` target.

**End state:** `make run-v2` runs without error, writes `runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl`, and the scaffold is ready for incremental implementation.

**Scope boundary:** `v2/shared/` = copied and adapted from v1. `v2/workers/` = written fresh.

---

## Why

- **v1 is deliberately broken**: 10 known bugs make it miss ~48 of ~50 matches. The fixes need a clean, purpose-built home.
- **Normalization and agent are the solution architecture**: the root cause is data normalization (resolve_job_town drops 99.6% of rows). `stage_normalise` + `stage_agent` is the right layering.
- **Shared independence**: `v2/shared/` diverges freely from v1/shared without breaking v1.
- **Scaffold first**: structure before logic — every stub is a placeholder for a specific bug fix.

---

## What

### Pipeline architecture

```
v2 STAGE_GRAPH
──────────────
stage_clean_jobs      load, dead-link filter, normalise rows, dedup
  load_job_feed
  filter_dead_links     ← NEW (fix bug #1: 404/410 jobs pass through in v1)
  normalise_job_rows
  drop_duplicate_jobs

stage_normalise       ← NORMALIZATION LEVEL
  resolve_location      ← fix bug #2: location string parsing
  resolve_title         ← fix bug #3: scraped title abbreviations
  resolve_company       ← fix bug #5: company name normalization

stage_agent           ← AGENT LEVEL (LLM fallback)
  (empty for now — implementation TBD)

stage_match_jobs
  match_jobs            ← fix bug #4: word-by-word title matching
  portal_matches_output
```

### New row fields added by v2 normalise stage

```python
# After stage_normalise, each row gains:
row["resolved_title"]    # str — best title found (stub: same as row["title"])
row["resolved_company"]  # str — normalized company (stub: same as row["company"])
row["town"]              # str — resolved UK town (same contract as v1 resolve_job_town)
row["region"]            # str
row["country"]           # str
row["used_llm"]          # bool — False initially
```

`match_jobs` reads `row.get("resolved_title", row["title"])` and `row.get("resolved_company", row["company"])` so stubs degrade gracefully.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] `make run-v2` exits 0, writes output file
- [ ] `make test` exits 0 — no regression in v1 tests
- [ ] `ruff check v2/ --fix` exits 0
- [ ] `python -c "from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult"` succeeds
- [ ] All v2 modules have: MODULE_NAME, MODULE_TYPE, REJECTION_REASONS, ERROR_REASONS, WARNING_REASONS, `main()`
- [ ] `tests/v2/__init__.py` exists (empty)

---

## All Needed Context

### Source files to READ (not copy — understand only)

```yaml
- file: v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py
  why: Defines ExecutionResult, StageDefinition, run_stage_loop, run_local_handler —
       these are the runtime primitives every module, stage and handler uses.
       v2/shared/ will be an adapted copy; v2/workers/ code imports from v2.shared.

- file: v1/shared/observability/sli_observe.py
  why: Defines passed(), reject(), sli_observe() — the observability contract
       every module must call sli_observe() ONCE at the end on ALL rows.

- file: v1/shared/patterns/logging.py
  why: get_logger(MODULE_NAME), log_event() — logging pattern every module follows.

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/load_job_feed.py
  why: REFERENCE for module contract structure (MODULE_NAME/TYPE/REASONS, main(), L1/L2 pattern)
       Write v2 version fresh — do not copy.

- file: v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/match_jobs.py
  why: REFERENCE for three-gate filter pattern (company → title → location).

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"COMPANY_NOT_LISTED", "NO_TITLE_MATCH", "NO_LOCATION_MATCH"}

import re

_LEGAL_SUFFIXES = re.compile(
    r"\s+(ltd|limited|plc|group|holdings|international|uk)\s*$", re.IGNORECASE
)

def _normalise_name(name: str) -> str:
    name = name.lower().strip()
    name = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", "", name)
    name = _LEGAL_SUFFIXES.sub("", name)
    name = re.sub(r"^the\s+", "", name)
    return name.strip()

def _words(title: str) -> set[str]:
    tokens = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", " ", title.lower()).split()
    # strip trailing plural 's'
    return {t.rstrip("s") for t in tokens}

def matched_titles(job_title: str, profile_titles: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Every word of each profile title must appear in job_title (any order, case-insensitive)."""
    job_words = _words(job_title)
    return [t for t in profile_titles if _words(t) <= job_words]

def matched_companies(job_company: str, profile_companies: set[str]) -> str | None:
    """Return the profile company name that matches (after suffix normalisation), or None."""
    norm_job = _normalise_name(job_company)
    for c in profile_companies:
        if _normalise_name(c) == norm_job:
            return c
    return None

def _towns_covered(location: dict) -> set[str]:
    """Profile location → set of town names it covers (inlined; no _shared dependency)."""
    return {location["name"], *location.get("includes", [])}

def main(context, prev_data):
    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    profile = context["profile"]
    profile_companies = {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}
    rows = [dict(r) for r in prev_data]   # copy so same rows can run multiple profiles
    for row in rows:
        job_company = row.get("resolved_company") or row.get("company", "")
        job_title   = row.get("resolved_title")   or row.get("title", "")
        matched_co = matched_companies(job_company, profile_companies)
        if matched_co is None:
            reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
            continue
        titles = matched_titles(job_title, profile["titles"])
        if not titles:
            reject(row, "NO_TITLE_MATCH")
            continue
        locations = [loc["name"] for loc in profile["locations"]
                     if row.get("town", "") in _towns_covered(loc)]
        if not locations:
            reject(row, "NO_LOCATION_MATCH")
            continue
        row["matched_company"]   = matched_co
        row["matched_job_title"] = titles
        row["matched_location"]  = locations
        row["reason"]            = f"{job_title} at {matched_co}, in {row.get('town', '')}"
    kept = passed(rows)
    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(trace_id=trace_id,
                           script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
                           data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={})

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"COMPANY_NOT_LISTED", "NO_TITLE_MATCH", "NO_LOCATION_MATCH"}

import re

_LEGAL_SUFFIXES = re.compile(
    r"\s+(ltd|limited|plc|group|holdings|international|uk)\s*$", re.IGNORECASE
)

def _normalise_name(name: str) -> str:
    name = name.lower().strip()
    name = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", "", name)
    name = _LEGAL_SUFFIXES.sub("", name)
    name = re.sub(r"^the\s+", "", name)
    return name.strip()

def _words(title: str) -> set[str]:
    tokens = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", " ", title.lower()).split()
    # strip trailing plural 's'
